parts.title: A METAL Strap? Design a School Bag Like an ENGINEER (Part 1) | The Design Process
parts.description:
A school bag with a torn strap: fabric, metal or wood? Look closer at three straps, then design the whole bag like an engineer, part by part: what it is for, its parts, the use of each part, a drawing, and a suitable material for each part. Be a book inside the bag! Part 1 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials: the design process.

In this part:
• Look closer: three straps over the back of a chair (flexible and strong)
• What engineers do
• The design steps: OUR DESIGN PLAN
• Look closer: one bag, four parts, four uses
• HOLD ON! Every part of fabric?
• Look closer: draw it, then choose (plastic base, metal zip, fabric straps)
• Be a book inside the school bag
• Spot the hidden butterfly, and a butterfly fun fact!

Key words: engineers, design, intended use.
Watch Part 2: we test the new strap, then design a zoo home! Last episode: why isn't a trolley made of glass? Choosing materials.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!

Singapore Primary 3 Science (2023 syllabus): Diversity of materials (Chapter 3, p. 66) and the Diversity theme closure (pp. 70-72). Design a school bag like an engineer. P3 Science, Chapter 3, Diversity of Materials, and the Diversity theme closure: what engineers do, the steps of the design process, how to design your own school bag, how engineers test a product, and why it is important to maintain diversity. Also fits US NGSS 3-5-ETS1-1 (Grade 3 to 5 engineering).
Safety: in this video an adult lifts the bag, adds the weights and does every test. We never force a material until it breaks. At the zoo we look, and we do not feed the animals.
Try it at home: design one object in your head. Pick one part. Tell someone at home what that part must do, which material you chose, and why.
Singapore and the US: in Singapore it is a school bag; in the US (Grade 3 to 5 engineering) it is a backpack, and pupils try the same design steps at the science fair. The science is the same: engineers choose materials by their properties, and then they test.

parts.title: We TESTED Our New Strap. Then We Designed a ZOO Home! (Part 2) | The Design Process
parts.description:
Will the new strap hold? The old strap held five weights, then it tore. Look closer at a fair test, be the new strap, then use the same design plan for a goat home at the zoo. Why is it important to maintain diversity? Part 2 of Primary 3 Science, Diversity of materials and the Diversity theme closure.

In this part:
• Look closer: the strength test (5 weights or 9?)
• After designing, engineers test their product
• Be the new strap
• Look closer: a goat home at the zoo (a wooden fence)
• Showdown: find the mistake in Basil's zoo map
• A great variety of living things: why it matters
• A chant to remember it all
• Spot the hidden frog, and a frog fun fact!

Key words: test, diversity, extinct.
Watch Part 1 first! Next episode: why does the Sun come back every morning?
